name: Sound_Bgm_Request
signature: void Sound_Bgm_Request(SoundBank* self, u32 index, u16 priority)
summary: Requests one BGM/sound entry by index (0..0xa4): increments the entry's use counter, clears its finished flag, resolves the sound group resource and queues the playback.
evidence: Guards 'self+4 & 1' (bank enabled) and index <= 0xa4; the record array is 0x24 bytes per entry; the two entries 0 and 1 default to priority 0xd (the BGM slots); 0x001ECA0C(self, record->f_110->f_4, 0) starts the stream, the f_f8/f_e0 bitmaps track which entries are active (index >> 5 word, 1 << (index & 31)); 0x001ED618(self,&record->f_110) resolves the resource and record->f_130 = priority; f_d8 counts active entries. Callers 0x001EC504/0x001EDAB4 (the sound driver).

signature: void maybe_Ui_Sequence_DeleteThunk(u32 a1, u32 a2, u32 a3, u32 a4)
summary: Deleting-destructor thunk for the sequence object; the real arguments reach it in r5/r6, so only the shape is recoverable.
evidence: Body is '0x001F201C(arg1,arg2,unaff_r6<<1,arg4,unaff_r5>>7); 0x0010F6CC()' - a tail position with a mangled register ABI, the same 0x0010F6CC delete suffix as 0x001F200C.

name: maybe_Ui_Sequence_Delete
summary: Deleting destructor of the sequence object: runs 0x001F201C and frees.
evidence: Two statements: 0x001F201C() then 0x0010F6CC(); the twin 0x001F2004 passes extra arguments instead, so both are deleting-destructor variants reached from vtables.

name: maybe_Ui_Sequence_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a wide sequence/panel object: releases the two leading objects and unwinds about twenty embedded list and text members.
evidence: Stamps *arg1 = g_001f21b4, releases arg1[0x15]/[0x16] with 0x0021F8B8, then a long series of 'unlink [n]/[n+1]' blocks with tags g_001f21b8/bc/c0/c4/c8 (the same member pattern as 0x001DDE38), ending in 0x001F29D4(arg1+7) -> 0x00261A9C(-0x18) -> this-4.

name: Ui_HandleSet_ValidateAndConvert
summary: Checks that all twelve referenced layout handles are loaded and then converts each one to the resolved object, marking the set as validated.
evidence: First loop over 9 handles at +4.., second over 3 handles at +0x28.., each probing the global handle table (g_001f22f8, generation in the high 12 bits) and requiring object state f_78 == 4; if all pass it calls 0x0071342C(&slot, prev) (resolve) for each and 0x00193FA0(obj) on a hit, then sets byte +1 = 1. Companion of 0x001F25D0/0x001F29D4 which build and retag the same 9+3 slots.

name: maybe_Ui_LoadLayoutByIndex
summary: Loads the layout resource for a row index (0..8, with 0x1b mapped to 8) and returns the loaded object's handler word.
evidence: Builds a 9-word copy of self->f_30..f_50, maps arg2 == 0x1b to 8, and for index < 9 resolves the name through the lazily built table (0x00293A00-style 0x98-byte singleton) and 0x00124E5C, then 0x00193FA0(obj,0) and returns **(u32**)(obj[0x24]+0x24); no callers (factory slot).

name: maybe_Ui_Array_InitThunk
signature: void maybe_Ui_Array_InitThunk(u32 a1, u32 a2, u32 a3, u32 a4)
summary: Degenerate thunk around 0x00100BE0 (the array-constructor helper) whose arguments live in r5/r6.
evidence: Body is a single '0x00100BE0(unaff_r5 + 4, arg2, unaff_r6 << 1, arg4, arg3, arg4)' call; 0x00100BE0 is the same constructor helper used with explicit sizes by 0x001F0700 and 0x001C9AE8. No callers.

name: Ui_HandleSet_Init12
summary: Builds the twelve resource handles of a UI layout set (nine row layouts plus three shared parts) by formatting their names and creating each object.
evidence: Two loops: 9 entries at +4 from the static name table _FUN_001F2958[0..8] and 3 entries at +0x28 from g_0072b540/44/48; each name is formatted with 0x006F0C10, the resource created with 0x003882F0 and the handle swapped in with 0x001241D0/0x00124DD0; the same slot layout is validated by 0x001F21CC.

name: maybe_Ui_HandleSet_Retag
summary: Retags all twelve handles of the set to the current resource generation and re-initialises the two arrays.
evidence: For each of the 9 + 3 slots it releases the old handle (generation mismatch check against g_001f2ac8/g_001f2acc) and rewrites 'handle & 0xfffff000 | g_001f2ac8<<12'; then 0x00100BE0(self+0x28, g_001f2ad0, 4, 3) and (self+4, ..., 4, 9); called from 0x001F201C's destructor chain and by the ABI thunk 0x001F2004.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_ResetPair
summary: When the widget's owner check succeeds, resets the two child widgets at +0x8e0 and +0x930.
evidence: Guarded by 0x00630B04(self, self+0x980); then 0x003E021C(self+0x930,0), 0x003E0088(self+0x8e0) and 0x003E043C(self+0x8e0,0) - the same part-reset trio used by the cursor/panel destructors.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_DtorChain
summary: Destructor chain for a widget: unwinds the member at +0x24c - 0x50 - 0x7a8, unlinks its nodes and frees.
evidence: 0x003E04BC(arg1+0x24c), then 0x001CA340(-0x7a8), stamps this-0x1c = g_001f43d0, unlinks two node pairs, then 0x001D8C2C(-0x138) and 0x0010F6CC; no callers.

name: maybe_Gfx_Scene_Init
signature: void maybe_Gfx_Scene_Init(GfxScene* self, u32 mode, u32 a3, u32 a4)
summary: Initialises one of the scene's two render paths (2D or 3D) and clears the scene's per-frame flags.
evidence: Clears the byte flags f_423c/f_423d/f_423e/f_424f/f_4d74, calls 0x002078C4 (sub-object creation), then either the f_4244 ('3D') path with 0x00168C18 + 0x00175840(&f_4330) or the default path with 0x00626A1C(work,1) + 0x00175840(&f_47a0). Callers 0x001A14EC and 0x001A1AA4; the companion 0x00207760/0x00208BE0 release the same members.

name: maybe_Gfx_Scene_Release
summary: Releases the scene's render path and the three optional sub-objects created by 0x002078C4.
evidence: Calls vtable +0x14(0) on self->f_10, then 0x001690FC on self+0x47a0 or self+0x4330 (chosen by f_4244), then vtable +0x24 + f_94 = 1 on f_431c, f_4320 and (3D path only) f_4324; caller 0x0019F4FC.

name: maybe_Gfx_Scene_CreateSubObjects
summary: Creates the scene's two (or, in 3D mode, four) helper objects and links the effect object to its emitter.
evidence: Allocates g_00207a84 -> 0x00269BC0 into f_431c and g_00207a88 -> 0x00282238 into f_4320; when f_4244 (3D) it additionally creates a 0x2d4-byte object (0x003248F0) into f_4324, links it with 0x0027C094(f_4320, obj->f_1a0) and a 0x268-byte object (0x00469FF4) into f_4328; called only from 0x00206BBC.

name: maybe_Gfx_Scene_Shutdown
summary: Shuts the scene down: tells every child drawable to hide, releases the render path, tears down the six helper objects and resets the scene's state byte.
evidence: Walks the list at f_4260 calling vtable +0x110(obj,1) when f_4248 is set (and sets f_b0fc = 1 on each when f_424a is set); then 0x006034BC + 0x00175808(&f_47a0) or 0x00606CEC + 0x00175808(&f_4330); releases f_431c/f_4320/f_4324/f_4328, calls 0x00626338(work), and writes 0xff into g_00208e00[self]; caller 0x0020E358 (the scene manager).

name: maybe_Gfx_Scene_CheckState
summary: Polls the scene's renderer: reports 'still busy' while a fade is pending and otherwise raises the renderer error code (0xe, or 8 when the optional flag is set) and lets the scene manager finish it.
evidence: If f_423d: returns 1 while *(int*)(f_10+8) < g_00209ee8, else writes the error pair (f_1200/f_1204 from g_00209eec) into the renderer and calls vtable +0x14(f_10, 0xe or 8); else it probes work->f_14->f_c's virtual +0x34 twice and, when both report, calls 0x0020E358(self) and sets g_00209ef0[self] = 1. Always returns 1.
